newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia peso falls amid record one-day trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombia peso falls amid record one-day trade.

text.p: Colombia's peso fell 1.04 to end the final session of the year at 1,004.93 to the dollar amid record one-day trade of $474 million, interbank traders said Monday.
Dealers said there had been frantic intervention by the central bank as it fought to stop the dollar plunging through the floor of the floating daily exchange rate band.
The central bank declined to give figures but traders calculated it had bought at least $400 million.
"There was a flood of a greenbacks onto the market after the recent privatizations, and also export revenues from the oil and coffee sectors," one dealer said.
Traders reported 152 operations worth $474 million, which they said was a one-day record.

The peso sank to an intraday low of 1,005.2 and closed at the high. Based on interbank rates, the peso has lost just 1.22 percent of its value in the course of 1996, compared to a government target of 13.5 percent devaluation.
The strong peso has led to a chorus of complaints from key export sectors, such as the coffee industry, as their goods become less competitive in the international marketplace.
